source: Dr. Thaveesak Sangudom, Dr. Theerawut Chutinanthakun, and Wirot Horasart, "Off-season Production Techniques for Pursat Orange (ក្រូចពោធិ៍សាត់ / kroch poursat) in Cambodia," in The Guideline of Climate Change Adaptation in Cambodia (pp. 130-153), Project on Promoting Climate Resilience in Farming Communities of Cambodia, General Department of Agriculture (GDA) Cambodia, Thailand International Cooperation Agency (TICA), and Department of Agriculture (DOA) Thailand, 2017-2020.
text:
Pruning is a key step in shifting Pursat orange (ក្រូចពោធិ៍សាត់) into off-season production. After the main harvest, farmers cut back old, damaged, and unproductive branches, including any branch growing inward toward the center of the tree rather than outward. This removes shelter used by pests, lets light and air move through the canopy more evenly, and pushes the tree to put out a fresh, synchronized flush of new growth.

In the demonstration orchard, pruning is scheduled for November (weeks 1-2 of the annual cycle), immediately after fertilizing and tending the trees following the prior season's harvest. A well-pruned tree is easier to maintain, uses less pesticide overall because it is less hospitable to pests, and responds better to the flowering-induction steps that follow (withholding and then resuming irrigation).
